starting_points.name: create-vite React TypeScript template
starting_points.when: A new browser React application backed by an existing or separately owned API.
steps: Choose a supported Node runtime and package manager; inspect create-vite help and template requirements.
Create in an unused local source directory with the official react-ts template, then install dependencies inside the generated project.
Record generator/runtime versions and template choice in README; use the generated lockfile for subsequent installs.

commands.cwd: A local source-workspace parent outside synchronized storage; my-app must not already exist
commands.purpose: Check Node against the resolved Vite/template requirements.

commands.purpose: Install generated dependencies and create the npm lockfile.

notes: Replace my-app with the unused intended directory. Preserve an established package manager in existing work.
This template creates the client application, not an API server, database, authentication service or production hosting setup. Do not put secrets or database credentials in browser code.

follow_up_generators.name: Feature generation boundary
follow_up_generators.when: Adding client components/routes or integrating the selected API after scaffolding.
notes: Vite does not provide a general component/model/controller generator. Use installed router/UI tooling only if the project has selected it; ordinary React components follow the generated module and TypeScript conventions.
Database migration generators belong in the API/backend repository that owns the data. Do not add PostgreSQL/Drizzle tooling to a browser-only bundle.

preserve: Generated .gitignore, index.html entry, Vite/React plugin setup, ESLint configuration, TypeScript project configuration and package scripts.
Lockfile and runtime constraints; adapt sample components while retaining the working scaffold.
verification: Run npm run build and the generated lint script; confirm build includes the template TypeScript check rather than relying on transpilation alone.
Run npm run dev and inspect the actual browser UI; test API origins/authentication at the browser boundary.
Review ignore behavior and generated-file deviations before adding project files.
integration_steps: Extend the generated README with API/session owners, API contract, run/check commands and environment variable names. Confirm strict TypeScript and add router/query tooling only when needed.

Add Zod when validating runtime input or external data is required, and configure the selected test tools. Implement error/loading/session-expiry states and verify authoritative authorization in the API that owns the data.

Build static assets, configure the chosen production host for deep links and API origins, and verify browser navigation plus authentication/session behavior against the deployed API during an authorized release.
